Question: Mr. Green measures his rectangular garden by walking two of the sides and finds that it is \(15\) steps by \(20\) steps. Each of Mr. Green’s steps is \(2\) feet long. Mr. Green expects a half a pound of potatoes per square foot from his garden. How many pounds of potatoes does Mr. Green expect from his garden?
Solution:
Convert both side lengths to feet before finding the area. Since each step is \(2\) feet, the garden measures
\[
15\cdot2=30\text{ feet}
\quad\text{by}\quad
20\cdot2=40\text{ feet}.
\]
Its area is \(30\cdot40=1200\) square feet. Each square foot yields half a pound, so the expected harvest is
\[
1200\cdot\frac12=\boxed{600\text{ pounds}}.
\]
The answer is \(\text{A}\).
